  and the race's results as your game showed them (each racer's time and how far they came). Its log keeps your report
  with your name, for evening out the cars, and names a racer who won by cheating. Nobody sees your real address: the
  server gives each player a virtual one (`10.77.x.x`).
- **A tab in the background** (or another window in front) pauses your game. The others see you as paused: your car
  stays where you stopped, with "paused" after your name. After 8 minutes in the background you stop playing with
  others and your place on the server is freed: your car disappears for them, and your next key, mouse move or button
  brings you back. The same happens after 12 minutes without a key, the mouse or a controller, after a 2-minute "Still
  there?" warning.
- **Closing the tab:** the others see your car disappear after a few seconds.
- **Messages over the game** say when a player joins free roam, is back in free roam after a race, starts a
  multiplayer race nearby, turns free roam off or loses the connection, and, for a player near you, goes into a race
  or quits. The menus and the shops are not announced, and nothing shows while you race.
- **The game's own LAN races** (its LAN menu) work between players on the same server too, with free roam on or off.

## 7. The game's Online mode

The game's own **Online** menu works again, against this server instead of EA's long-gone one: everyone who plays
from the same server address can meet there.

1. Main menu, **Online**. You go straight to the Online Main Menu under your name: **Online, Your name** on the
   start page, or your profile name when that is empty. There are no EA accounts, so the game's EA Login screens are
   skipped.
2. **Lobby** shows the games. **Create Game** (race type, track, options; Game Type Unranked), or **Refresh** and
   **Join Game**. In the game room, chat, press **Ready**; the creator presses **Start Race**. When only some
   players are ready, Start Race counts down 10 seconds: whoever is still not ready then is removed from the game,
   and the race starts without them.

Good to know:

- **Your name** keeps letters, digits, `-` and `_` (3 to 15), online and in free roam alike: `Alex K.` plays as
  `Alex_K`. A changed name applies the next time you press Play.
- **A name that reads as a slur** is not taken: Settings does not save it as **Your name**, the Online mode
  refuses it, and in free roam the other players see `Player` over your car. Digits or signs for letters (`1` for
  `i`), gaps and repeated letters read as the word they spell; a number (a year, two digits at the end) is a number
  (`Hakan1995` and `Dani99` are names). The same goes for Nazi names (and `1488` in a name), hate aimed at a group,
  terror and sexual violence. Swear words are fine.
- **Chat in the Lobby and in a game room** is read the same way, word by word: a line with a slur in it reaches no
  one but you, and after three of them in ten minutes you cannot chat for ten minutes. Swear words are fine. A player
  you block in EA Messenger is not heard there either. In the race itself and on its results, quick chat's set
  phrases work (1 to 4, then 1 to 4; section 6, Quick chat).
- **Submit Complaint** (choose a player in a game room) tells the server's operator about that player, with their
  last few chat lines (of the last ten minutes) that you could see; the operator decides what happens. Without a
  complaint no chat is written down anywhere, only the word that kept a line from the others.
- **Your name is yours once you claim it.** **Online, Your name** says what your name is: free, claimed by you,
  or another player's. **Claim** there claims it with your passphrase (the one of your cloud saves), after a check from
  Cloudflare that a person, not a script, claims it (usually it passes by itself). Without a passphrase, Claim makes
  one and turns cloud saves on, then shows it to keep: it is the only way to play under the name again, in another
  browser or after this browser's data is cleared, and the only way back to your saves. With a passphrase that has
  no name yet, Play claims a free name by itself; Cloudflare's check shows only when it wants a click.
  - One name: once your passphrase holds a name, you always play as it, whatever Your name says. Another name you
    type there is played only after **Change name**, and the line under Your name says which name you play as. With
    the box empty, you play as your claimed name too.
  - While it is yours nobody else plays under it: in the Online menu and in free roam they get your name with four
    digits added (`Alex` becomes `Alex4821`; a name longer than 11 characters loses its end to them), the same
    digits each time for their browser. If someone was online under it before you came, the lobby gives it back to
    you.
  - It stays yours as long as your passphrase does: until you delete your cloud saves, or they go unused for two
    years. In another browser, load your passphrase under Cloud saves and the name is yours there too.
  - One name a passphrase. **Change name** (type another name) changes it once a week; the old name stays yours for
    14 more days, and your friends move to the new one (their lists show it).
  - `NAME`, the game's default profile name, and `Player` can't be claimed: Play asks once for a name of your own,
    and until you pick one you play as `NAME` with your four digits. A name another player claimed: Play asks once
    for another, and you play as it with your digits until then. Neither applies offline or with the network off, nor
    with a claimed name of your own (you play as that one).
  - A name that reads as a slur can't be claimed (the rules below).
  - Without a claim your name is anyone's: whoever is online under it first keeps it (the others get digits), and
    EA Messenger keeps no lists for it: your friends, blocked players and requests last until you leave Online.
- **No name and no profile:** the game's own EA Login screens come instead. **Use Existing EA Account**, any name
  (3 to 15 letters, digits, `-` or `_`) and any password, **Continue**; **No** to "create a profile"; your persona.
  Nothing is checked and nothing is kept: there are no accounts. Type a password you use nowhere else: the game
  sends it to the server only lightly scrambled (the server never reads it).
- **Kept on the server:** only race results per name (Rankings; a name not seen for a year is forgotten), the claimed
  names (each with a code made from its passphrase, never the passphrase, and when it was claimed and last played or
  used: kept as long as the passphrase), and the EA Messenger lists of claimed names, with their passphrase's code: your friends and the
  players you block (names), the friend requests you sent until they are answered (30 days at most), and your
  friends' messages that came while you were away until you are back (7 days at most). Lists of names nobody claimed
  are kept only while their player is online; the lists kept before names could be claimed went to the first
  passphrase that claims each name (the ones of `NAME` and `Player`, which hundreds of players shared, were deleted).
  Of chat, only your last five lines, for ten minutes and in memory, for a complaint. Never your password: the server
  does not read it.
- **Game passwords:** the game asks for the password of a game created with one, and only the same password joins
  it. The server keeps no copy of it, only a check value for that game while it is open, and never shows or logs it.
- **Others see** your name, your game, your chat and your results, never your real address.
- **Every track is open** when you create a game, either direction, whatever your career has unlocked, and a new
  game starts at **2 laps** (the game's own default was 3; Options, Laps changes it). A drift game takes **2 laps** or
  more, as a circuit, ranked too (the game's own least was 4). The same goes for the game's LAN races. The career and
  Quick Race keep their unlocks.
- **Up to 6 players** race in one game (Options, Max Players; the game's own most was 4, and 6 only in URL races).
  Drag keeps one car per lane: 4, or 3 on the track with three lanes.
- **Horn:** N (or the controller's left stick click) honks in a race too, as in free roam: the others hear the horn you
  picked from your car. The same in the game's LAN races.
- **The Lobby lists every open game**, whatever its race type and options (Collision Detection, Race Breaker, Car
  Performance Restrictions, Ranked), those its **Filter** asks for first, until you set the Filter: after Apply
  Filter (or Back) on its screen it lists only the games the Filter asks for. Set the Filter back to its defaults
  (Circuit, no restriction, both options on, Unranked) to see every game again. A game you create or join gives the
  Filter its own settings (the original game does that), and the list is the whole one again until you next set it.
  In the original game the Filter always hid all others, so a game made with Collision Detection off was seen by no
  one. A game with **Private Room** on is not listed, as in the original game.
- **Ranked games** need three players at least. Ranked races give ranking points by place. After a ranked race the
  results screen lists whose results came in (received or waiting), then, once the games of two players sent the
  same finishing order, Official Race Results: each player's place, time (drift: score) and the ranking points the
  race gave (100 for the winner down to 0 for the last; 0 for a player who did not finish, shown as Disconnected:
  who left the race, or was still on the way when it ended, 30 s after the first finisher).
- **A race counts** in Rankings once the games of two players who raced to the end (finished, or were still on the
  way when the race ended) sent the same finishing order (every game sends its own at the results screen), so a race
  counts even when only its winner finished. A player who left the race decides nothing: their game counts every
  player as gone. Each player races from their own browser. **Monthly Point Leaders** (Online Main Menu) shows this
  month's two leaders of each race type and, on its other page, last month's (from 1 December 2026, with November's
  leaders first: the server kept no whole month before it).
- **EA Messenger** (the Online Main Menu's button): Search finds the players online on this server and those with a
  race in Rankings. **Send Friend Request** reaches the other player now, or when they next come online: they see you
  in their list with a green arrow and pick **Answer Friend Request**: Accept, Decline or Block. Your friends stay on
  your list and are told when you come online; **Remove Friend** takes the two of you off each other's lists. A
  message to a friend who is not in Online mode reaches them in free roam or on the start page (see Messages to
  friends), or waits for them (7 days) and shows with an envelope when they are back; a message to anyone else reaches
  them only while they are online. A message with a slur in it reaches no one, as in the Lobby's chat. Players you block stay blocked: nothing of theirs reaches
  you.
- **Who is on:** Playing now on the start page (under Play) shows how many play on this server now, how many of
  them are in Online mode (in its lobbies or racing) and how many in free roam. Only numbers: no names.
- Turning it off: Online, More online settings, Online mode on the start page (the game then cannot connect).

## 8. When something is wrong

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Secure, isolated page" on another PC, `PAGE-NOT-SECURE` | Open the server's `https://` address, not `http`. Only `localhost` works without HTTPS. |
| `PAGE-NOT-ISOLATED` ("Something in this browser changes the page"; before 4 November "not cross-origin isolated"), and with it `MODULE-NOT-ISOLATED` | The page is not opened from the game's server, or something in the browser changes it on the way, most often an extension. A guest or private window shows whether that is it (its saves are gone when it closes); then, in a normal window, turn the extensions off one by one. |
| `PAGE-NO-MEMORY`: "Shared WebAssembly memory is not available" | The browser cannot give the game the memory it needs. Close other tabs, update the browser and restart it. |
| `PAGE-NO-JIT`: "The JavaScript optimizer is off for this site" (or "exnref not supported by the Wasm interpreter") | The browser runs WebAssembly without its compiler here, and the game cannot run that way. Chrome: Settings, Privacy and security, JavaScript optimization and security: allow the site (Android's Advanced Protection turns the optimizer off for every site). Edge: add the site as an exception to Enhanced security. |
| `PAGE-NO-WAITASYNC`: "This browser is too old for the game" | Update the browser (Firefox 145 or newer), or play in Chrome. |
| `PAGE-NO-SIMD`: "This computer's processor is too old for the game" | The game needs WebAssembly SIMD: a PC processor without SSE4.1 (an AMD Phenom II, an Intel Core 2 before Penryn) or a browser too old for it can't compile the game. Update the browser; on such a processor the game can't run. |
| "Graphics (WebGPU)", `GPU-OFF` and the other `GPU-OFF-…` | The browser has no WebGPU, which the game needs. Chrome: update it (on Linux also turn on `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu`). Firefox has it on Windows and on Macs with Apple chips; elsewhere (Linux, Macs with Intel chips) play in Chrome, or set `dom.webgpu.enabled` to true in about:config. Firefox for Android has none yet: play in Chrome. iPhone and iPad: WebGPU comes with iOS 26 and iPadOS 26. `GPU-NOT-SECURE`: see "Secure, isolated page" above. |
| `GPU-ACCEL-OFF` | Chrome uses no graphics at all (it draws WebGL in software, or not at all): "Use graphics acceleration when available" in `chrome://settings/system` is off, or Chrome gave up on the graphics after they crashed. Turn it on and restart Chrome; if it was on, update the graphics driver. |
| `GPU-ADAPTER-LINUX`: Chrome on Linux, while `chrome://gpu` says WebGPU is hardware accelerated | Most likely the Vulkan driver is missing: Chrome runs WebGPU on Vulkan there (the rest of Chrome on OpenGL). `ls /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/` lists the installed ones (`intel_icd` for Intel, `radeon_icd` for AMD). Install it with `sudo apt install mesa-vulkan-drivers` on Debian and Ubuntu, `sudo dnf install mesa-vulkan-drivers` on Fedora, `vulkan-intel` or `vulkan-radeon` on Arch, then quit Chrome completely and start it again. Chrome has WebGPU on by itself on Linux for Intel graphics (Gen12 and newer) and NVIDIA (Wayland); for other graphics turn on `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu`. If the driver is there, the Dawn Info section further down `chrome://gpu` lists each adapter WebGPU sees and why one is blocked. |
| `GPU-ADAPTER-WIN`: Chrome on Windows | Chrome runs WebGPU on Direct3D 12 there, and older graphics have no Direct3D 12 driver (Intel HD 4000, 4400, 4600 and older, for one): the game cannot run on that computer. The Dawn Info section further down `chrome://gpu` lists each adapter WebGPU sees and why it is blocked; when it lists only "D3D11 backend" adapters, "Blocklisted - D3D11 backend not fully implemented", the graphics have no Direct3D 12. On newer graphics, update the graphics driver from Intel, AMD or NVIDIA, then quit Chrome completely and start it again. |
| `GPU-ADAPTER-WIN-ARM`: Chrome on Windows on ARM (Snapdragon) | Chrome keeps WebGPU behind a flag there: turn on `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu`, then restart Chrome. |
| `GPU-ADAPTER-ANDROID` | Chrome on Android has WebGPU from Android 12 on Qualcomm (Adreno), ARM (Mali) and Intel graphics, and from Android 16 on Imagination (PowerVR). Update Android and Chrome. If that does not help, turn on `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu` (on the phone, type it into Chrome's address bar, or open `chrome://flags` and search for "Unsafe WebGPU"), then restart Chrome: that lifts Chrome's WebGPU blocklist. Samsung's Xclipse (some Galaxy phones) is on it, and the game runs with the flag (a player's Xclipse 540 with Android 16). If the game still does not run with it, it cannot run on that phone yet. |
| `GPU-ADAPTER`, `GPU-ADAPTER-FIREFOX` | The browser would not use the graphics. Restart it; update the graphics driver (on a Mac: macOS) and the browser. `chrome://gpu` in Chrome, about:support (Graphics) in Firefox says why. In Firefox on Windows, graphics without Direct3D 12 cannot run it either. |
| `GPU-ADAPTER-AFTER-LOST` | The graphics stopped during the last game (`GPU-LOST`), and the browser has not given the reloaded page graphics since: not graphics too old. Chrome keeps a site whose graphics hung off them for a while (two minutes); the page asks again every 10 seconds, and Play comes on once they are back. If it stays off, quit the browser completely (every window) and start it again. If the graphics stop again, update the graphics driver; two players' Intel Iris Xe hung this way (`DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG` in the log). |
| `GPU-SOFTWARE`: a note that the graphics are software | Chrome gave the game its processor's stand-in for graphics (SwiftShader), which it does with `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu` where it cannot use the graphics: the game runs at ~13 fps. On Linux (a Steam Deck's Chrome, for one), turn on `chrome://flags/#enable-vulkan` and `chrome://flags/#default-angle-vulkan` and restart Chrome (a player's fix: `--enable-features=Vulkan --use-angle=vulkan`). Elsewhere, see `GPU-ACCEL-OFF`. |
| `GPU-NO-BC`: a note about packed textures | Nothing to do: the game plays. These graphics can read neither of the texture formats the game uses, so the page unpacks the textures as the game loads: about 200 MB more memory, and loading screens may pause for a moment. Graphics that can read ASTC (iPhones, iPads, most phones) get no note: most textures are converted to that, about 50 MB more. |
| `GPU-INTEGRATED-FIREFOX`: "Graphics: Intel (integrated)" (or AMD) in Firefox on Windows | Firefox runs the game on the graphics it draws its own windows with, whatever the game asks for. If the computer also has a graphics card, as many laptops do, give Firefox the card: Windows Settings, System, Display, Graphics, Firefox, High performance; then quit Firefox completely and start it again. On a computer with integrated graphics only, nothing changes. Chrome does the same (its `chrome://gpu` names the graphics it uses): the same Windows setting for Chrome, or `chrome://flags/#force-high-performance-gpu`. |
| `GPU-RENDERER`: "The game was stopped" | The graphics did not start: the game cannot go on without them. Restart the browser and press **Play**; if it happens again, update the graphics driver, and download the log (its `[gpu]` lines say why). |
| `GPU-ANDROID-DRIVER`: "Did not start" | The phone's graphics driver refused the game's picture at its first frame (Chrome on some phones with Adreno 6xx graphics; the log's `[gpu] device lost` line says `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` while "checking external image import support"). Every Play ends the same way on that phone: no setting changes it. A system update for the phone (a newer graphics driver) may; another browser on Android has no WebGPU yet. |
| `GPU-LOST`: "The game was stopped" | The graphics stopped during the game (the graphics driver reset, or the browser's graphics process crashed): the game cannot go on without them. Press **Play**: the page reloads, which starts the graphics again (Safari gives a page no graphics after that until it reloads), then **Play** starts the game. Your saves and settings stay. Download the log first if you want to keep it: after the reload, Download log has only a shorter copy of that game's. If the page then says `GPU-ADAPTER-AFTER-LOST`, see that. If it keeps happening, restart the browser and update the graphics driver. |
| "Game module", `MODULE-LOAD`: "The game didn't load" | The game did not load, or the server is not reachable (the log says why). The page tries again by itself, or press **Retry**. If the module is missing, start the server with `web/start.sh`, which builds it. |
| "A new version is out" | During a game: quit when it suits you (F9, **Quit game**). On the start page, press **Reload** or **Play**: the page loads the new version, and your saves and settings stay. Download the log first if you want to keep it: after the reload, Download log has only a shorter copy of that game's. Before any game the page reloads by itself; during a game it says so over the game, and the start page offers it when you quit. |
| "Open elsewhere" | The game runs in another tab of this browser. Switch to it, or close it. |
| "Not loading": "Your antivirus or network is probably blocking the game" | The page's own script never started, 15 seconds after the page opened: an antivirus (Kaspersky flagged the site in November 2026) or a network filter blocks it. Allow `nfsu2.xyz` in it, or try mobile data, then **Reload**. |
| "The game's files didn't load properly" (error code 1 in the first minute) | The game's program file did not load: the browser's copy is damaged, or the network blocks it (the log shows `no PE signature`, or `HTTP 403` for it). **Game**, **Delete game data** (at the tab's end), then **Play**; your saves stay. If it happens again, try another network. |
| `GAME-START`: "Did not start", "The game couldn't start" | Press **Play** again; if it happens again, **Download log** (on the start page) and post the log with the message. "This device doesn't have enough free memory for the game" (the log: "could not allocate memory" in Chrome, "Out of memory" in Safari): the browser would not set aside the game's 1 GB, most often on phones with 2 to 4 GB (a 32-bit Chrome, an iPhone's Home Screen app). Close other apps and reload the page; the log's `[memory]` line says what the browser refused. |
| `STORAGE-NONE`: "This browser window cannot store files" | A guest or private window cannot keep saves: open the page in a normal window. |
| `STORAGE-OLD`: "This browser is too old for the game" | Safari before 26 (iOS 18 with Safari's WebGPU feature flag on, for one) cannot write the game's files. Update to iOS 26, iPadOS 26 or macOS with Safari 26 (Settings, General, Software Update). |
| `SAVES-UNREADABLE`: "Play without saving?", "This browser can't read or write your saves right now" | The browser's storage for the site answered the page with an error (the message names it; Firefox says `UnknownError: Unknown failure`, a full disk among the causes). Nothing of the saves was written or removed. **Play without saving** starts the game anyway: it reads what it can, and nothing from that game is kept (no profile, setting or screenshot). Otherwise restart the browser, make sure the disk has free space, and press **Play** again. If it still fails and the message says your cloud saves have your progress: copy or download your passphrase first (**Cloud saves**; Firefox and Safari keep it only in the site's data), then remove this site's data in the browser's settings (Firefox: Settings, Privacy & Security, Cookies and Site Data, Manage Data; screenshots, covers, this device's settings, the Put back copy and the downloaded game data go too), reload, and enter the passphrase under **Cloud saves**. Otherwise don't remove it (that deletes what the cloud doesn't have) and ask on Discord. Shown over a game: the browser refused a file the game saves to, so a save may not have been kept. |
| `STORAGE-ASK`: the browser asks whether the site may keep its data | Allow it, so that your saves stay when the disk runs low (section 5). |
| `BROWSER-CHROME-OLD`, `BROWSER-FIREFOX-OLD` | A warning: the game may still play. Update the browser (Chrome 140 or newer, Firefox 145 or newer). |
| `BROWSER-OTHER` | A warning: the page does not know this browser (it knows Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Firefox and Safari). It may work when every other check passes. |
| `BROWSER-IPHONE` | Not a problem: on an iPhone the page cannot go full screen, but its copy on the Home Screen can (section 2). |
| `VAULT-…`: a cloud saves problem | The message says what happened: `VAULT-WRONG-KEY` (these saves do not open with this passphrase: check it), `VAULT-TOO-LARGE` (more than the server keeps), `VAULT-HTTP-429` (too many tries: wait a minute), `VAULT-HTTP-503` and `VAULT-HTTP-507` (the server takes no more saves for now), `VAULT-NO-ANSWER` and `VAULT-TIMEOUT` (the server did not answer: try again), `VAULT-LOAD-HALFWAY` (loading the cloud's saves stopped halfway: load again before playing; the copy the page kept of yours is under Put back). |
| No sound | Click the game or press a key. Check the sound setting and the output latency (try "Robust"). |
| Stuck on a loading screen | F9, Quit game; then "Close the game now"; then "Stop the game". When the log ends in `[data]` lines, the game was waiting for its data from the server: it goes on when the data comes. |
| Other players' cars stutter, freeze and jump in an Online or LAN race | The game's own updates go through the player who created the game (the other players' cars also come straight from their games, and small corrections are smoothed out), so let whoever has the steadiest connection (a cable rather than Wi-Fi or mobile) and the fastest computer create it, and keep the game's tab in front. A connection that stops for a second or more still makes cars jump when it comes back. After the race, F9, Download log: its `[racenet]` lines say how each car's updates came (long waits, how many came at once after them) and each player's frame rate. |
| Anything odd | F9, Download log (or "Download log" on the start page after the game ended) and keep the file. It has the game's own log. When the browser stopped the page itself (on an iPhone the game is suddenly gone and the page loads again), the start page says so and Download log starts with that last game's log. After you reload or close the page during a game, Download log has that game's log as well. It names your browser, its version and your system, your graphics chip, and your time zone's offset from UTC. Names (yours, your profiles', crews' and room's, and those of the players you met) and addresses become stand-ins such as `you`, `player-3k9x` and `vlan-7q2m`, the same in every log from that browser, so you can post it as it is. |
| `Port 8080 is in use` when starting | The server already runs; open its address. Or start on another port: `web/start.sh --http-port 9080`. |
| Full screen | The game plays in the browser window. F9, Full screen goes full screen, and holding Esc leaves it (in Firefox, a press). "Full screen on Play" (Game, Display) starts every game full screen. |

#!/bin/bash
# Regenerate everything derived from SPEED2.EXE: relocs, lifted C, import args.
#   ./gen.sh [path/to/SPEED2.EXE]      (default: $NFSU2_DATA/SPEED2.EXE)
# The OVERRIDE list is derived from the runtime sources (every sub_X_orig the
# runtime references, plus the DX_WRAP(...) table in d3dx_hle.c), so it can
# never drift out of sync with runtime/overrides.c + runtime/d3dx_hle.c.
# When it has finished, gen/all/stamp.txt (and gen/server/stamp.txt) say what
# the lift was made from (tools/genstamp.sh): hashes of the override list,
# the hook list and the lifter, the exe, and the lift options; a build can
# then refuse a gen/all that is older than its runtime (web/build.sh does).
set -e
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"
EXE="${1:-${NFSU2_DATA:+$NFSU2_DATA/SPEED2.EXE}}"
[ -f "$EXE" ] || { echo "usage: ./gen.sh path/to/SPEED2.EXE"; exit 1; }
PY="$ROOT/.venv/bin/python"
# no stamp until this run has finished; web/gen.sh's label is for its own runs only
mkdir -p gen/all
rm -f gen/all/web-lift.txt
echo "incomplete: gen.sh has not finished (or failed)" > gen/all/stamp.txt
STAMP_SOURCES="$(tools/genstamp.sh sources)"
OV=$(tools/genstamp.sh overrides)
echo "OVERRIDE ($(echo "$OV" | tr ',' '\n' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')): $OV"
# Instruction hooks (guest_hook before the instruction): every HOOK_SITE(0x...)
# in the runtime sources, plus any extra HOOKS=... given for debugging.
HK=$( { tools/genstamp.sh hooks | tr ',' '\n'; echo "$HOOKS" | tr ',' '\n'; } | grep -E '^0x' | sort -u | paste -sd, -)
echo "HOOKS ($(echo "$HK" | tr ',' '\n' | grep -c .)): $HK"
# x87 precision control (tools/lift.py): on by
# default, so the game thread computes at PC=24 like on Windows; X87PC=0
# lifts plain doubles (the code before this option).
export X87PC="${X87PC:-1}"
echo "X87PC=$X87PC"
"$PY" tools/reloc2.py "$EXE"
OVERRIDE="$OV" HOOKS="$HK" "$PY" tools/genall.py "$EXE" "${NSHARD:-128}"
"$PY" tools/argcount.py "$EXE" > out/argcount.log
echo "gen OK -> gen/all ($(ls gen/all/shard_*.c | wc -l | tr -d ' ') shards)"

# Second guest module: EA's LAN server, server.dll next to SPEED2.EXE, lifted
# at the fixed guest base 0x00A00000 (runtime/module.c maps the original file
# there and checks its SHA-256 against the one recorded in gen/server).  The
# exe's output above does not depend on it.  Without server.dll a stub module
# is generated: the build links, and hosting a LAN game reports "unavailable".
SRV="$(dirname "$EXE")/server.dll"
mkdir -p gen/server && find gen/server/ -mindepth 1 -delete   # empties it; a worktree's link to the shared one stays a link
if [ -f "$SRV" ]; then
  "$PY" tools/prepare_module.py "$SRV" 0x00A00000 out/server gen/server srv_
  GENOUT=gen/server RELOCS=out/server/relocs.txt SEEDS=out/server/seeds.txt SYMPFX=srv_ \
    OVERRIDE="$OV" HOOKS="$HK" "$PY" tools/genall.py out/server/image.dll "${NSHARD_SRV:-8}" > out/server/genall.log
  grep -E "functions  *:|traps \(|truncated|MISSING" out/server/genall.log | sed 's/^/  server.dll: /'
  RELOCS=out/server/relocs.txt IMPOUT=gen/server/impargs.c SYMPFX=srv_ STRICT=1 IMPDLL="$SRV" \
    "$PY" tools/argcount.py out/server/image.dll > out/server/argcount.log
  echo "gen OK -> gen/server ($(ls gen/server/shard_*.c | wc -l | tr -d ' ') shards)"
else
  mkdir -p gen/server
  printf '#include "module.h"\nconst ModInfo g_srv_modinfo = { "server.dll", "", 0x00a00000u, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 };\n' > gen/server/modinfo.c
  printf '#include "cpu.h"\ntypedef void(*guest_fn)(CPU*);\nconst uint32_t g_srv_fn_count = 0;\nconst uint32_t g_srv_fn_addr[1] = {0};\nconst guest_fn g_srv_fn_ptr[1] = {0};\n' > gen/server/fntab.c
  printf '#include <stdint.h>\ntypedef struct { uint32_t iat; const char*dll; const char*name; int nargs; } ImpEnt;\nconst uint32_t g_srv_imp_count = 0;\nconst ImpEnt g_srv_imp[1] = {{0}};\n' > gen/server/impargs.c
  printf '#ifndef DECLS_H\n#define DECLS_H\n#include "cpu.h"\n#endif\n' > gen/server/decls.h
  echo "gen: no $SRV -> stub gen/server (LAN hosting unavailable in this build)"
fi

# what this lift was made from (tools/genstamp.sh; the source lines are compared by web/build.sh)
h16(){ shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-16; }
STAMP="$(echo "# gen.sh $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ): what gen/all and gen/server were lifted from"
  echo "$STAMP_SOURCES"
  echo "exe $(h16 < "$EXE")$( [ -f "$SRV" ] && echo " server.dll $(h16 < "$SRV")")"
  echo "options X87PC=$X87PC X87OPT=${X87OPT:-} JTSWITCH=${JTSWITCH:-} LREGS=${LREGS:-} FTOL2INL=${FTOL2INL:-} FLAGABI=$( [ -z "${FLAGABI:-}" ] && echo - || { [ -f "$FLAGABI" ] && h16 < "$FLAGABI" || echo missing; } )" \
       "FLAGOPT=${FLAGOPT:-} RETEIP=${RETEIP:-} INLINE=${INLINE:-} INLINE_LIST=$( [ -z "${INLINE_LIST:-}" ] && echo - || basename "$INLINE_LIST") NOCLOSURE=${NOCLOSURE:-} COMMENTS=${COMMENTS:-}" \
       "WATCH=${WATCH:-} COVERAGE=${COVERAGE:-} NSHARD=${NSHARD:-128}/${NSHARD_SRV:-8} HOOKS=${HOOKS:-}")"
echo "$STAMP" > gen/server/stamp.txt
echo "$STAMP" > gen/all/stamp.txt

END TEXT OBJECT AT000470

BEGIN TEXT OBJECT
{"id": "AT000476", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/link.sh", "originalBytes": 8845, "originalSha256": "ea73f4ce9f1d0e38e1a190072dc4549bd60599ed38ea0f8302f7bd06bc5c25a7", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 8845, "utf8TotalBytes": 8845}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/bin/bash
# Compile the runtime and link the binaries (the shards must already be compiled)
#
# TWO SEPARATE BUILDS are made; the lifted shards are SHARED, only the runtime differs:
#   out/nfsu2_boot     the port: the game's own look by default; the optional
#                      graphics (msaa, mirror, texture_filtering, graphics
#                      preset) are runtime options, all off by default
#   out/nfsu2_hd_boot  research build (NFS_ENHANCED=1): the larger road
#                      reflection, upstream's SSR and ray-traced reflections,
#                      HD_* defaults.  Not packaged (measured and
#                      rejected)
#   out/nfsu2_all      test suite (with the original runtime)
#
#   ./link.sh          both
#   ./link.sh orig     original only
#   ./link.sh hd       HD only
set -e
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"
MCPU="${MCPU:-apple-m1}"; MINOS="${MINOS:-11.0}"   # see build.sh
OPT="${OPT:--O3 -mcpu=$MCPU -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS}"
LDOPT="${LDOPT} -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS"
WHICH="${1:-both}"
case "$WHICH" in both|orig|hd) ;; *) echo "usage: ./link.sh [orig|hd]"; exit 1 ;; esac

CSRC="mem dispatch genexec heap watchdog win32 win32_ext com debug features res fileio overrides d3dx_hle vsemu enhance perflog autotest lifecycle widescreen framerate dinput_pad dikeys keyboard dinput_kbd career intro oracle drifttest discord roam roam_core roam_bsd roam_game mprace mpcredit horn hornmenu optslider tonemenu radio powerunits drift carsfx racehorn racenet racecars winsock online netrace net_vlan module modheap headlights language sms sponsors lobbyclick olfilter tunegraph dyno menusize regional garage sndlead carshadow carpaint hiddenraces visualrep hqvinyls whine carspot walls travel movie photo look savegame uniques catchup showoff quickrace cameras vinylcat vinylpacks modpacks specialties lightkey plates plate_image trafficcars shownames hudbank engage gpsdistance stance"
CSRC="$CSRC splitscreen coop damage_none"   # damage_none: the crash damage is the browser build's (damage.c)
MSRC="metal audio bundle gamepad keyboard_mac fpscounter texrep"
# Unicorn 2.1.4 (native arm64, x86 target only) for the two test builds,
# ORACLE=1 and ASIPEER=1: by default the project's work/deps/unicorn-2.1.4
# (its README.txt says where it came from and how it was built), found from
# two folders above the checkout (../../work/deps or ../../deps).
# UNICORN_INC=<src>/include and UNICORN_LIB=<build>/libunicorn.a override it.
UDEP=""
for d in "$ROOT/../../work/deps/unicorn-2.1.4" "$ROOT/../../deps/unicorn-2.1.4"; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && { UDEP="$(cd "$d" && pwd)"; break; }
done
UNICORN_INC="${UNICORN_INC:-${UDEP:+$UDEP/include}}"; UNICORN_LIB="${UNICORN_LIB:-${UDEP:+$UDEP/lib/libunicorn.a}}"
# ORACLE=1: test binary with the differential x87 oracle (runtime/oracle.c).
ORACLE_CFLAGS=""; ORACLE_LIBS=""
if [ "${ORACLE:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  [ -f "$UNICORN_LIB" ] && [ -d "$UNICORN_INC" ] || { echo "ORACLE=1 needs Unicorn: work/deps/unicorn-2.1.4, or UNICORN_INC and UNICORN_LIB"; exit 1; }
  ORACLE_CFLAGS="-DNFSU2_ORACLE -I$UNICORN_INC"; ORACLE_LIBS="$UNICORN_LIB -lpthread"
fi
FW="-lm -framework Cocoa -framework Metal -framework QuartzCore -framework ImageIO -framework CoreGraphics -framework CoreServices -framework AudioToolbox -framework CoreAudio -framework GameController -framework Carbon"
SHARDS="$(ls gen/all/shard_*.c | sed -E "s|gen/all/(.*)\.c|out/obj/\1.o|" | tr "\n" " ") out/obj/fntab.o $([ -f gen/all/stubs.c ] && echo out/obj/stubs.o || true)"
# server.dll (gen.sh -> gen/server, build.sh -> out/obj/srv); a stub module
# when the game folder had no server.dll at gen time
[ -f gen/server/fntab.c ] || { echo "gen/server is missing: run ./gen.sh"; exit 1; }
SHARDS="$SHARDS $(ls gen/server/shard_*.c 2>/dev/null | sed -E "s|gen/server/(.*)\.c|out/obj/srv/\1.o|" | tr "\n" " ") out/obj/srv/fntab.o $([ -f gen/server/stubs.c ] && echo out/obj/srv/stubs.o || true)"

# $1 = object directory, $2 = NFS_ENHANCED value.  Files compile in parallel.
build_rt(){
  local od="$1" enh="$2" pids="" f
  mkdir -p "$od"
  for f in $CSRC; do
    [ -f "runtime/$f.c" ] || continue
    # roam_core, roam_game: no fused multiply-add, so their floats are
    # bit-identical to the x86 build of the same files (the Windows companion,
    # win/roam_asi)
    local fx=""; case "$f" in roam_core|roam_game) fx="-ffp-contract=off" ;; esac
    clang $OPT $fx -DNFS_ENHANCED=$enh $ORACLE_CFLAGS -Iruntime -Igen/all -c -o "$od/$f.o" "runtime/$f.c" & pids="$pids $!"
  done
  for f in $MSRC; do
    clang $OPT -DNFS_ENHANCED=$enh -fobjc-arc -Iruntime -Igen/all -c -o "$od/$f.o" "runtime/$f.m" & pids="$pids $!"
  done
  clang $OPT -Iruntime -Igen/all -c -o "$od/impargs.o" gen/all/impargs.c & pids="$pids $!"
  clang $OPT -Iruntime -c -o "$od/srv_impargs.o" gen/server/impargs.c & pids="$pids $!"
  clang $OPT -Iruntime -c -o "$od/srv_modinfo.o" gen/server/modinfo.c & pids="$pids $!"
  clang $OPT -DNFS_ENHANCED=$enh -Iruntime -Igen/all -c -o "$od/boot.o" tests/boot.c & pids="$pids $!"
  for p in $pids; do wait "$p" || { echo "compile error ($od)"; return 1; }; done
}
rt_objs(){ local od="$1" f o=""
  for f in $CSRC $MSRC impargs srv_impargs srv_modinfo; do [ -f "$od/$f.o" ] && o="$o $od/$f.o"; done
  echo "$o"; }

if [ "${ORACLE:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  # oracle test binary only: own objects, own name, the normal build untouched
  build_rt out/obj_oracle 0                  # enhance.o too: the options are in every build
  RT="$(rt_objs out/obj_oracle)"
  clang ${LDOPT} -o out/nfsu2_oracle $SHARDS $RT out/obj_oracle/boot.o $FW $ORACLE_LIBS
  echo "link OK: oracle (out/nfsu2_oracle)"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$WHICH" != hd ]; then
  build_rt out/obj 0
  RT="$(rt_objs out/obj)"
  clang $OPT -Iruntime -Igen/all -c -o out/obj/main.o tests/main_all.c
  clang ${LDOPT} -o out/nfsu2_boot $SHARDS $RT out/obj/boot.o $FW
  clang ${LDOPT} -o out/nfsu2_all  $SHARDS $RT out/obj/main.o $FW
  # free-roam multiplayer core: unit tests (./run.sh test runs them)
  clang -O1 -ffp-contract=off -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS -Iruntime -o out/roam_unit tests/roam_unit.c runtime/roam_core.c runtime/roam_bsd.c
  clang -O2 -ffp-contract=off -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS -Iruntime -o out/roam_fakepeer tests/roam_fakepeer.c runtime/roam_core.c runtime/roam_bsd.c
  clang -O2 -ffp-contract=off -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS -Iruntime -o out/roam_recv tests/roam_recv.c runtime/roam_core.c runtime/roam_bsd.c
  # ASIPEER=1: also out/nfsu2_asipeer, a "virtual Windows friend" (the Windows
  # plugin out/win/dbg/NFSU2FreeRoam.asi under Unicorn, runtime/roam_asipeer.c;
  # test tooling) and the plugin's tests (tests/asi_harness.c,
  # tests/roam_pe_selftest.c).  Unicorn: as for ORACLE=1 above.
  if [ "${ASIPEER:-0}" = 1 ]; then
    UINC="$UNICORN_INC"; ULIB="$UNICORN_LIB"
    [ -f "$ULIB" ] && [ -d "$UINC" ] || { echo "ASIPEER=1 needs Unicorn: work/deps/unicorn-2.1.4, or UNICORN_INC and UNICORN_LIB (now: '$UINC', '$ULIB')"; exit 1; }
    for f in tests/asi_vm tests/asi_win32 runtime/roam_asipeer; do
      clang $OPT -Iruntime -Itests -I"$UINC" -c -o "out/obj/$(basename $f).o" "$f.c"
    done
    clang ${LDOPT} -o out/nfsu2_asipeer $SHARDS $RT out/obj/asi_vm.o out/obj/asi_win32.o out/obj/roam_asipeer.o out/obj/boot.o "$ULIB" $FW -lpthread
    clang -O2 -g -ffp-contract=off -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS -Iruntime -Itests -I"$UINC" -o out/asi_harness tests/asi_harness.c \
      tests/asi_vm.c tests/asi_win32.c runtime/roam_game.c runtime/roam_core.c "$ULIB" -lpthread -lm
    clang -O2 -ffp-contract=off -mmacosx-version-min=$MINOS -Iruntime -Itests -I"$UINC" -o out/roam_pe_selftest tests/roam_pe_selftest.c \
      tests/asi_vm.c tests/roam_selftest.c "$ULIB" -lpthread -lm
    echo "link OK: out/nfsu2_asipeer, out/asi_harness, out/roam_pe_selftest (Unicorn)"
  fi
  # Winsock / Netbios HLE unit harness (./run.sh test runs it)
  clang -O1 -Iruntime -o out/net_harness tests/net_harness.c runtime/winsock.c runtime/net_vlan.c runtime/mem.c
  echo "link OK: original (out/nfsu2_boot)"
fi
if [ "$WHICH" != orig ]; then
  build_rt out/obj_hd 1
  RT="$(rt_objs out/obj_hd)"
  clang ${LDOPT} -o out/nfsu2_hd_boot $SHARDS $RT out/obj_hd/boot.o $FW
  echo "link OK: HD (out/nfsu2_hd_boot)"
fi

# ISA semantics tests
# Do NOT PASS SILENTLY if the generator fails.  The error used to be swallowed:
# while isatest.py crashed for weeks, the old gen/isatest.c was compiled and
# said "439 passed", so the tests never exercised the current lifter at all.
# Now the stale binary is deleted, so ./run.sh test fails visibly.
if "$ROOT/.venv/bin/python" "$ROOT/tools/isatest.py" >/dev/null \
   && clang -O1 -Wno-unused-label -Iruntime -o out/isatest gen/isatest.c runtime/mem.c -lm; then
  :
else
  rm -f out/isatest
  echo "WARNING: the ISA tests could not be generated/compiled -- out/isatest deleted" >&2
fi

END TEXT OBJECT AT000476

BEGIN TEXT OBJECT
{"id": "AT000477", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/pack.sh", "originalBytes": 8617, "originalSha256": "d6c81532bdd22a70199a37c1964a39220c3393100571ae8fd3f6d103d66453f5", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 8617, "utf8TotalBytes": 8617}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/bin/bash
# Build out/NFSU2.app from the linked binary.
#
#   ./pack.sh [--exe <SPEED2.EXE>] [--install [<dir>]]
#
# The separate "NFSU2 HD.app" is retired: its features that held up in the
# measurements (MSAA, the larger mirror, anisotropic filtering) are options
# of NFSU2.app, off by default (settings.ini "graphics = enhanced" or the
# single keys).  Its larger road reflection, ray-traced reflections and SSR
# stay in the unshipped research build (./link.sh hd -> out/nfsu2_hd_boot).
#
# The app holds only the port.  It runs against the user's own game folder,
# which it asks for on first launch and never writes to; registry, saves and
# settings live in ~/Library/Application Support/NFSU2, logs in
# ~/Library/Logs/NFSU2.
#
# The icon is made at build time from SPEED2.EXE's own icon resource, so the
# exe is needed here: --exe, else $NFSU2_DATA, else game_folder from the
# user's settings.ini, else the work/gamedata clone next to the checkout.
# --install copies the finished app to <dir> (default ~/Applications).
set -e
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"

EXE=""; INSTALL=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --hd)      echo "pack.sh --hd: the HD app is retired; NFSU2.app has the graphics options"
               echo "  (settings.ini: graphics = enhanced)."
               echo "  The research build out/nfsu2_hd_boot (./link.sh hd) is not packaged."
               exit 1 ;;
    --exe)     EXE="$2"; shift ;;
    --install) INSTALL="$HOME/Applications"
               case "$2" in ""|--*) ;; *) INSTALL="$2"; shift ;; esac ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

BIN="$ROOT/out/nfsu2_boot"; NAME="NFSU2"; DISP="Need for Speed Underground 2"
BID="org.nfsu2.nativeport"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "build first: ./build.sh && ./link.sh  ($BIN missing)"; exit 1; }

# arm64 only: the lifted code is AArch64 C, there is no x86 slice to fall
# back to (and Rosetta is not involved anywhere).
# LAN hosting needs server.dll lifted into the binary (gen.sh did that if the
# game folder it was given had server.dll; the app never contains the DLL
# itself and loads the user's own copy, checked by SHA-256, at run time).
ls "$ROOT"/gen/server/shard_*.c >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || echo "warning: gen/server has no lifted server.dll: hosting a LAN game will not be available in this app"
ARCHS="$(lipo -archs "$BIN")"
[ "$ARCHS" = "arm64" ] || { echo "expected an arm64-only binary, got: $ARCHS"; exit 1; }

BEGIN TEXT OBJECT
{"id": "AT000480", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/runtime/audio.m", "originalBytes": 36836, "originalSha256": "b42ccf1f9d0dd05f1e5147e9f69da7966b3ad6f9d125c8654652d7ce285fd518", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 36836, "utf8TotalBytes": 36836}
